name: 4.1.1_table_0
description: Guidelines for pump installation (page 18)

name: Make sure that the space around the unit is sufficient.
description: This facilitates ventilation, inspection, maintenance, and service.

name: If you require lifting equipment such as a hoist or tackle, make sure that there is enough space above the pump.
description: This makes it easier to properly use the lifting equipment and safely remove and relocate the components to a safe location.

name: Protect the unit from weather and water damage due to rain, flooding, and freezing temperatures.
description: This is applicable if nothing else is specified.

name: Do not install and operate the equipment in closed systems unless the system is constructed with properly-sized safety devices and control devices.
description: Acceptable devices: Pressure relief valves, Pressure controls, Temperature controls, Flow controls. If the system does not include these devices, consult the engineer or architect in charge before you operate the pump.

name: Take into consideration the occurrence of unwanted noise and vibration.
Make sure that the unit location is on solid, level ground.
description: This ensures that the unit remains stable and balanced while in operation.

name: Check that all piping is supported independently of, and lined up naturally with, the pump connection.
description:
This helps to prevent:
• Strain on the pump
• Misalignment between the pump and the drive unit
• Wear on the pump bearings, seal, and shafting
See Example section for illustrations of pipe supports.

name: Check that only necessary fittings are used.
description: This helps to minimize friction losses.

name: Make sure that all the piping joints and fittings are airtight.
description: This prevents air from entering the piping system or leaks that occur during operation.

name: If the pump handles corrosive fluids, make sure that the piping allows you to flush out the liquid before you remove the pump.
description: This protects the employees and operators.

name: Check that the distance between the inlet flange of the pump and the closest elbow is at least four pipe diameters.
description: This minimizes the risk of cavitation in the suction inlet of the pump due to turbulence.

name: Check that elbows in general do not have sharp bends.
Check that the eccentric reducer at the suction flange of the pump has the following properties: • Sloping side down • Horizontal side at the top
If suction strainers or suction bells are used, check that they are at least three times the area of the suction piping.
description: Suction strainers help to prevent clogging.

name: If more than one pump operates from the same liquid source, check that separate suction‑piping lines are used for each pump.
description: This recommendation helps you to achieve a higher pump performance.

name: If necessary, make sure that the suction piping includes a drain valve and that it is correctly installed.
Make sure that the suction piping is free from air pockets.
description: This helps to prevent the occurrence of air and cavitation in the pump inlet.

name: Check that the suction piping slopes upwards from the liquid source to the pump inlet.
Check that all joints are air-tight.
Check that an isolation valve is installed in the suction piping at a distance of at least two times the pipe diameter from the suction inlet
description: This permits you to close the line during pump inspection and maintenance. Do not use the isolation valve to throttle the pump. Throttling can cause loss of priming, excessive temperatures, damage to the pump, and voiding the warranty.

name: Check that the piping is level or slopes downward from the liquid source
Make sure that the size of the entrance from the supply is one or two sizes larger than the suction pipe
Make sure that the suction piping is adequately submerged below the surface of the liquid source
description: This prevents air from entering the pump through a suction vortex.
